chunks.arabic_text: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ إِسْمَاعِيلَ، عَنِ الْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ، عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ، عَنِ هِشَامِ بْنِ الْحَكَمِ وَغَيْرِهِ، عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ قَالَ

translations.en: Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

chunks.arabic_text: خَطَبَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ وَسَلَّمَ بِمِنَى فَقَالَ: أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ مَا جَاءَكُمْ عَنِّي يُوَافِقُ كِتَابَ اللَّهِ فَأَنَا قُلْتُهُ وَمَا جَاءَكُمْ يُخَالِفُ كِتَابَ اللَّهِ فَلَمْ أَقُلْهُ

translations.en: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) addressed the people in Mina and said: O people, whatever comes to you attributed to me which agrees with the Book of Allah then I have indeed said it, and whatever comes to you opposing the Book of Allah then I never said it.

en.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) delivered a sermon in Mina establishing a criterion for verifying his sayings: any narration that aligns with the Quran is authentic to him, while any that contradicts the Quran is not. This hadith serves as a foundational principle in Shia hadith sciences for validating prophetic traditions against the Quran.
en.seo_question: How do we verify if a hadith is truly from the Prophet based on the Quran?
